title: uml-mcp: letting an AI draw the diagram

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You type one sentence into a chat, something like draw me a sequence diagram of a user logging in through an API gateway, and a finished diagram appears right in the conversation. How does that work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'd have guessed the AI just draws a picture. Is that not it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not quite. The assistant writes the diagram as text, in a notation like PlantUML, Mermaid or D2. Then it calls a tool, and that tool is uml-mcp, a Model Context Protocol server. It sends back an image, a link to the rendered file and a link to an editable playground.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the AI writes the recipe and the server cooks it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's a good way to say it. In clients that support MCP Apps, the diagram even opens in a viewer inside the chat. In the demo, one batch call returns four diagrams as tabs, and you switch between them or re-render one in another format.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How many kinds of diagrams are we talking about?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The README counts forty-six types. Thirty-seven are rendered by Kroki, a diagram service, and nine come from four bundled plugins, including architecture and workflow diagrams and cloud diagrams with real logos.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what does the assistant actually get to call?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Five tools. One renders a diagram, one returns it as an inline image, one validates the source first with errors that say how to fix it, one lists the available types, and one renders several diagrams in a single call.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What happens behind the scenes when I ask for a diagram?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The server checks the type and the arguments, then looks in a cache so a repeated request comes back fast. If it isn't cached, it renders it. Kroki types go through the service, plugin types render locally. And if Kroki fails, PlantUML and Mermaid sources can be retried on other renderers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. It's on PyPI as uml-mcp, there's a hosted endpoint on Vercel, and you can self-host with Docker or Helm. The repository has ready-made configurations for Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop and others.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's even an admin side, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A web console with live logs, metrics and rate limits. So you describe the diagram and it shows up in the chat. The full write-up has the demo video and the step by step pipeline.
